as_told.title: Norton AFB meeting: Air Force asks Emenegger and Sandler to make a UFO documentary
as_told.place_text: Norton Air Force Base, California; the Pentagon

plain: The story is that in the early 1970s US military officials approached two film producers, Allan Sandler and Robert Emenegger, and asked them to make a documentary about UFOs. They even offered footage said to have been shot at Holloman Air Force Base. The online researcher UAPGerb says the pair "were approached by two US military officials" and could include the Holloman footage, and he names an officer called Weinbrenner. Michels tells it on the show with the contact running through Norton Air Force Base, where "everybody there is talking to him about UFOs." He ties it to the 1974 film UFOs: Past, Present and Future, which involved the astronomer J. Allen Hynek and the TV host Rod Serling. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron, who repeats what Emenegger told him, puts the meeting at Norton around 1973. He names a Norton official, Paul Shartle, a Colonel Coleman, and Nixon's chief of staff H.R. Haldeman. He says the officials asked for "this other documentary on UFOs" but wanted it hidden "below the other eight documentaries." If true, the military was trying to prepare the public for UFOs through a film it quietly encouraged.
